prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a compact kitchen with a counter crossing the foreground and a microwave and small appliance above it; the bright counter and appliances are roughly 0.3–1.2 m from the camera, while the floor and doorway extend about 1–3 m away. A partly visible person or arm appears at the lower edge in frames 2–4, within about 0.3–0.8 m, and two people appear beyond the counter area in frame 5 at roughly 1–2.5 m, although their separation and facing direction are poorly resolved. Across frames 1–4 the viewpoint turns right while remaining near the counter, making the microwave shift from upper centre-right to upper left; frame 5 reveals more of the room and the people on the right. The depth map makes near-versus-far surfaces and partial foreground occlusions clearer than RGB, but boundaries bleed, thin objects disappear, and the dark people in frame 5 appear implausibly distant, so metre estimates are only approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks isolate a remote on the left in frame 1, partial people near the lower edge in frames 2–4, a small region labelled dog in frame 4, and two overlapping people on the right in frame 5; most counters, appliances, floor, and walls are unlabelled. The lower-edge person masks are about 0.3–0.8 m from the camera and partly outside the image, while the two frame-5 people are approximately 1–2.5 m away, side by side and partially occluding one another; their exact facing and gaze cannot be established from these masks. The repeated lower-edge masks move from right-of-centre toward centre as the camera turns, and the frame-5 masks show one person left/in front of the other, with the rightmost body cut off by the image boundary. Segmentation clarifies instance separation and otherwise subtle occlusion, but labels such as “laptop,” “dog,” and “vase” conflict with the RGB appearance or cover implausible regions, and many prominent objects are missed.
descriptions.pose: Only frame 5 contains a detected yellow body skeleton, located on the nearer left person at the far right of the strip; no reliable body or hand skeleton appears in frames 1–4. The detected person is roughly 1–2 m in front of the camera and close to the second person, probably within about 0.3–0.8 m laterally, but the sparse joints do not establish gaze or precise facing. The skeleton suggests an upright torso with one arm extending downward-left, making limb orientation easier to see than in the blurred RGB, while the adjacent person and lower-edge figures remain undetected. Missing joints, small disconnected points, no magenta hand detections, overlap between the two people, and edge truncation make reach, occlusion, and motion across the five frames unreliable.
